quotes.text: མཐའ་དཔྱད་པ་ལ། མངོན་ཤེས་ཀྱི་རྟེན། བརྟེན་པ་མངོན་ཤེས་ཀྱི་རང་བཞིན། ས་མཚམས། རྒྱུ། དགོས་པ། ཁྱད་པར་དང་དྲུག་ལས།
quotes.why: Chökyi Gyaltsen's own six-point excursus on the clairvoyances; its sixth point, ཁྱད་པར, is what this paragraph's དྲུག་པ་ནི closes.

quotes.file: Tengyur/03 SHES PHYIN_Perfection of Wisdom (Prajñā Pāramitā)/VOL 12 (NA)/TD03807-1_SHES RAB KYI PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA 'BUM PA RGYA CHER 'GREL PA (Śatasāhasrikā Prajña Pāramitā Bṛhaṭṭīkā)_unicode.txt
quotes.citation: Śatasāhasrikā Bṛhaṭṭīkā (TD03807), vol. NA, gloss on the Śatasāhasrikā's list of what a bodhisattva who wishes for them should train in the perfection of wisdom
quotes.why: The passage the yig cha cites as ཡུམ་གྱི་གནོད་འཇོམས, in the canonical commentary itself; note ཐུགས where the yig cha reads མཐུ, and ལ་སོགས་པས་གོང་མ where it reads ལ་སོགས་པ་ས་གོང་མ. Found by direct search.

quotes.file: Tengyur/03 SHES PHYIN_Perfection of Wisdom (Prajñā Pāramitā)/VOL 12 (NA)/TD03807-1_SHES RAB KYI PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA 'BUM PA RGYA CHER 'GREL PA (Śatasāhasrikā Prajña Pāramitā Bṛhaṭṭīkā)_unicode.txt
quotes.citation: Śatasāhasrikā Bṛhaṭṭīkā (TD03807), vol. NA, the sentence introducing the same gloss
quotes.why: In its home context the superiority is claimed for bodhisattvas of the tenth ground, and for five clairvoyances, a qualification the yig cha does not carry over. Found by reading around the canonical passage.

quotes.file: Tengyur/03 SHES PHYIN_Perfection of Wisdom (Prajñā Pāramitā)/VOL 12 (NA)/TD03807-1_SHES RAB KYI PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA 'BUM PA RGYA CHER 'GREL PA (Śatasāhasrikā Prajña Pāramitā Bṛhaṭṭīkā)_unicode.txt
quotes.citation: Śatasāhasrikā Bṛhaṭṭīkā (TD03807), opening verse of homage
quotes.why: The commentary names itself གནོད་འཇོམས in its own opening verse, which is why Tibetan authors cite it as the 'Gnod 'joms of the Hundred Thousand'.
Tsongkhapa sets the Abhidharmakośa rule, that clairvoyance reaches only its own and lower levels, immediately before the Gnod 'joms quotation.

quotes.file: Tengyur/07 MNGON PA_Higher Knowledge School (Abhidharma)/VOL 2 (KU)/TD04089_CHOS MNGON PA'I MDZOD KYI TSIG LE'UR BYAS PA (Abhidarmakoṣa Kārikā)_unicode.txt
quotes.citation: Abhidharmakośa-kārikā (TD04089), chapter 7, verses on the six abhijñā
quotes.why: The canonical Kośa line Tsongkhapa is citing: the first five clairvoyances have their own and lower levels as object.
Tsongkhapa's third point on the clairvoyances cites the same passage as 'the Gnod 'joms of the Hundred Thousand'; the yig cha reuses his citation as its sixth point.
Jamyang Zhepa (Gomang) turns the same Gnod 'joms passage into a pervasion in a debate on the definition of other-mind clairvoyance; OCR is damaged in this line.
The root verse whose words མཐོང་ལམ་དང་། ། the paragraph takes as its lemma, the ninth of the ten instructions.

quotes.text: བཞི་པ་ལ། མཐོང་ལམ་ལ་གདམས་པ་དང་། སྒོམ་ལམ་ལ་གདམས་པ་གཉིས་ལས། དང་པོ་ནི། མཐོང་ལམ་དང་། ། ཞེས་བཤད།
quotes.why: Chökyi Gyaltsen's own earlier division of the ten instructions, which puts the path of seeing under 'instruction on the cause of the culmination of practice'.
Ārya Vimuktisena is the Indian source of the phrase སྒྲུབ་པ་མཐར་ཐུག་པའི་རྒྱུ that the paragraph applies to the path of seeing.
Haribhadra's gloss on མཐོང་ལམ་དང་། ། at the aligned place; the yig cha quotes it in the next paragraph as its བསྟན་བཅོས་ཀྱིས་འགྲེལ་ཚུལ།

quotes.citation: Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā, Part 1 (vol. KA), opening of chapter 3, immediately after the colophon of the Śāriputra chapter
quotes.why: The sūtra passage the paragraph opens its range with, in the 25,000-line sūtra the Ornament follows; the sūtra has སྤོབས་པ་སྐྱེད་ཅིག where the yig cha has སྤྱོད་པར་གྱིས་ཤིག. Found by direct search.

quotes.file: Kangyur/3. NYI KHRI (Perfection of Wisdom in 25,000 Lines (Pañca Viṃśati Sāhasrikā Prajñā Pāramitā)/VOL 1 (KA)/KL00009E1INC_SHES RAB KYI PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA STONG PHRAG NYI SHU LNGA PA 1_The Perfection of Wisdom in 25,000 Lines, Part 1 (Pañca Viṃśati Sāhasrikā Prajñā Pāramitā 1)_unicode.txt
quotes.citation: Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā, Part 1 (vol. KA), chapter 3, Subhūti's question
quotes.why: Subhūti's question that opens the sixteen sūtra sections, with the word ཚིག་བླ་དྭགས the yig cha keeps and Haribhadra's eight-chapter recension does not.

quotes.file: Kangyur/3. NYI KHRI (Perfection of Wisdom in 25,000 Lines (Pañca Viṃśati Sāhasrikā Prajñā Pāramitā)/VOL 1 (KA)/KL00009E1INC_SHES RAB KYI PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA STONG PHRAG NYI SHU LNGA PA 1_The Perfection of Wisdom in 25,000 Lines, Part 1 (Pañca Viṃśati Sāhasrikā Prajñā Pāramitā 1)_unicode.txt
quotes.citation: Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā, Part 1 (vol. KA), chapter 3, the last of the sixteen sections and the sentence that follows
quotes.why: The sūtra's closing line for the path of seeing runs straight on into 'Why? Because…', which the tradition cuts off and assigns to the path of meditation. Found by direct search.
Haribhadra's twenty-five-thousand in eight chapters: the source of the yig cha's phrase ཉེ་བར་འགོད་པ for the introductory section.
Ārya Vimuktisena assigns the paragraph's final sūtra line to the sixteenth moment, subsequent knowledge of the path, and closes the path-of-seeing instruction there.
Tsongkhapa: the Eight-Chapter and Vimuktisena agree on the introductory section, and then one sūtra section is applied to each of the sixteen moments; the yig cha's two-part layout follows this.
Bhadanta Vimuktisena explains why an instruction that is 'not the domain of hearers' is spoken by the hearer Subhūti: by the Buddha's blessing.
Panchen Sonam Drakpa (Loseling) runs the same syllogism the yig cha runs in p423, citing the sūtra with སྤོབས་པ་སྐྱེད་ཅིག, as the Kangyur has it.
